newsitem.title: UK: Dlr draws breath after drop on intervention remark.
newsitem.headline: Dlr draws breath after drop on intervention remark.

text.p: The dollar was trading steadily against the mark and yen by midday in Europe, with the market trying to find its feet after recent hectic ups and downs.

The market was using an influential Japanese official's comment that Tokyo would intervene in the market when the timing was effective -- a remark that drove dollar/yen down overnight --- as an opportunity to consolidate, traders and analysts said.
"The dollar came off quite a bit in Tokyo. Certainly Europe seemed unhappy with that level... and it's been nudging higher," said Pat Magill, head of corporate trading at Daiwa Europe.

"No-one seems to be displeased at the level it's (the dollar) at, the comments seem to be directed at the speed at which it's been moving rather than anything else," said HSBC James Capel economist David Bloom.

Analysts said Sakakibara's comment carried more weight when combined with that of Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer, who said on Wednesday that he expected the "normalisation" of the mark against the dollar to end soon and that the mark will remain a strong currency.

"I think we're getting to the stage where not just Japan but the U.S. and Germany are saying that this far is fine but any further would probably be problematic," said Francis Breedon, foreign exchange economist at Lehman Brothers.

Breedon said that even U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin's remark overnight that the U.S. policy on the dollar has not changed -- a comment that had bolstered the dollar overnight -- could be interpreted as a watering down of his recent comments that a strong dollar was in the U.S. interest.

However, analysts said the dollar's underlying sentiment was still firm. Today's moves meant the market was lying low ahead of key events such as Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to a Senate panel today, a Federal Open Market Committee next week and a meeting of G7 finance ministers and central bank governors early next month, they said.
"There's the G7 meeting coming up, and I think people are scared of trying to push the dollar too far and making a nasty communique come out against it," HSBC James Capel's Bloom said.

Elsewhere, the mark was mixed against other European currencies. It was at session highs against the French franc after the Bank of France cut its intervention rate to 3.10 percent from 3.15. The mark was at 3.3752/56 francs against 3.3729/34 late on Wednesday.
Sterling was steady on the dollar and mark in choppy trade. Cable was at $1.6198/08 against 1.6208/18, while sterling/mark was at 2.6585/95 versus 2.6600/10.
